questions.stem: Solubility of $\mathrm{Ca_3(PO_4)_2}$ is ' S ' $\mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$. Find solubility product.
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{Ca_3(PO_4)_2 \rightleftharpoons 3Ca^{2+} + 2PO_4^{3-}}$, so $[\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}] = 3S$ and $[\mathrm{PO_4^{3-}}] = 2S$.
Step 2: $K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}]^3[\mathrm{PO_4^{3-}}]^2 = (3S)^3(2S)^2 = 27S^3 \times 4S^2 = 108S^5$
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{108\,S^5}$
Quick Tip: For $\mathrm{A_xB_y}$, $K_{sp} = x^x y^y S^{x+y}$.

questions.stem: Which from following reagents is used in Gatterman-Koch formylation of arene?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In the Gattermann-Koch reaction, benzene (arene) is treated with carbon monoxide and HCl in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ (with CuCl).
Step 2: CO and HCl generate the formyl cation equivalent that attacks the ring: $\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CO + HCl \xrightarrow{anhyd.\ AlCl_3/CuCl} C_6H_5CHO + HCl}$. ($\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$ is the Etard reagent; DIBAL-H reduces esters/nitriles.)
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{CO, HCl}$ (anhyd. $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$)
Quick Tip: Gattermann-Koch = CO + HCl; Etard = $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$ on toluene.

questions.stem: Which of the following species acts as reducing agent during working of hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Anode: $\mathrm{2H_2 + 4OH^- \rightarrow 4H_2O + 4e^-}$; cathode: $\mathrm{O_2 + 2H_2O + 4e^- \rightarrow 4OH^-}$.
Step 2: $\mathrm{H_2}$ is oxidised (0 to +1) and gives electrons, so it is the reducing agent; $\mathrm{O_2}$ is reduced and is the oxidising agent.
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{H_2}$
Quick Tip: The species oxidised at the anode is always the reducing agent.

questions.stem: The rate constant for a first order reaction is $0.58\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$ at 300 K and $0.026\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$ at 290 K . What is the energy of activation? $\left(\mathrm{R = 8.314\ J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}\right)$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Arrhenius equation: $\log\frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{E_a}{2.303R}\left(\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right)$, with $k_2 = 0.58$ at $T_2 = 300$ K and $k_1 = 0.026$ at $T_1 = 290$ K.
Step 2: $\frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{0.58}{0.026} = 22.31$, $\log 22.31 = 1.3485$; $\frac{T_1 T_2}{T_2 - T_1} = \frac{290 \times 300}{10} = 8700\ \mathrm{K}$
Step 3: $E_a = 2.303 \times 8.314 \times 1.3485 \times 8700 = 2.246 \times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{J} \approx 224.6\ \mathrm{kJ}$
Final Answer: (B) 224.55 kJ
Quick Tip: Keep the higher k with the higher T so $E_a$ comes out positive.

questions.stem: The reaction of propane with bromine in presence of UV light predominantly forms
questions.solution:
Step 1: Photobromination is a free-radical substitution; bromine radical is very selective and abstracts the H that gives the most stable radical.
Step 2: Removing a $2^\circ$ H gives the more stable secondary radical $\mathrm{CH_3\dot{C}HCH_3}$, so 2-bromopropane is the major product: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_3 + Br_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} CH_3CHBrCH_3 + HBr}$.
Final Answer: (B) 2-Bromopropane
Quick Tip: Bromination is far more selective than chlorination for $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$ hydrogens.

questions.stem: Which of the following pair of compounds on heating gives butanenitrile?
questions.solution:
Step 1: KCN gives $\mathrm{CN^-}$, which displaces halide from an alkyl halide ($S_N2$) and adds one carbon to the chain. Alcohols do not react since $\mathrm{OH^-}$ is a poor leaving group.
Step 2: Butanenitrile has 4 C including the CN carbon, so a 3-carbon halide is needed: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2Cl + KCN \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CH_2CN + KCl}$.
Final Answer: (D) n -Propylchloride and alcoholic KCN
Quick Tip: R-X + KCN gives R-CN with one more carbon; n-butyl chloride would give pentanenitrile.

questions.stem: Standard potential $(\mathrm{E^\circ})$ of $\mathrm{Zn^{+2}_{(aq)} + 2e^- \longrightarrow Zn_{(s)}}$ is -0.76 V . What is standard potential of reaction $\mathrm{2Zn_{(s)} \longrightarrow 2Zn^{+2}_{(aq)} + 4e^-}$?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Reversing the reduction half reaction to oxidation changes the sign: $E^\circ_{\mathrm{ox}} = +0.76$ V.
Step 2: Electrode potential is an intensive property, so multiplying the equation by 2 does not change it. $E^\circ = +0.76$ V.
Final Answer: (D) +0.76 V
Quick Tip: Reverse the reaction: change sign; multiply the reaction: E stays the same (unlike $\Delta G$).

questions.stem: Identify the ligands present in cisplatin.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Cisplatin is cis-diamminedichloridoplatinum(II), $\mathrm{cis\text{-}[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]}$, a square planar anticancer drug.
Step 2: Its ligands are two $\mathrm{NH_3}$ molecules and two $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ ions.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$
Quick Tip: Cisplatin = $\mathrm{cis\text{-}[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]}$, used in cancer chemotherapy.

questions.stem: Identify false statement from the following about fluorine.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Fluorine is the most electronegative element, shows only $-1$ oxidation state and forms only one oxoacid, HOF. So (A), (B), (D) are true.
Step 2: Bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{F_2}$ (about 158 kJ/mol) is lower than that of $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ (242) and $\mathrm{Br_2}$ (192), because the small F atoms have strong lone pair-lone pair repulsion. Order: $\mathrm{Cl_2 > Br_2 > F_2 > I_2}$. So (C) is false.
Final Answer: (C) It has high bond dissociation enthalpy among all halogens.
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{Cl_2}$, not $\mathrm{F_2}$, has the highest bond dissociation enthalpy among halogens.

options.text: It has high bond dissociation enthalpy among all halogens.

questions.stem: Which from following process involves zero work done?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Pressure-volume work is $W = -P_{ext}\Delta V$.
Step 2: In free expansion the gas expands into vacuum, so $P_{ext} = 0$ and $W = 0$. In the other processes the gas works against (or is worked on by) a non-zero pressure.
Final Answer: (D) Free expansion of gas.
Quick Tip: Expansion against vacuum: $W = 0$ always.

questions.stem: Calculate the constant external pressure required to expand 2 moles of an ideal gas from volume $\mathrm{15\,dm^3}$ to $\mathrm{20\,dm^3}$ if amount of work done is -600 J .
questions.solution:
Step 1: $W = -P_{ext}\Delta V$, with $\Delta V = 20 - 15 = 5\ \mathrm{dm^3} = 5 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$.
Step 2: $-600 = -P_{ext} \times 5 \times 10^{-3} \Rightarrow P_{ext} = \frac{600}{5 \times 10^{-3}} = 1.2 \times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa}$
Step 3: $1\ \mathrm{bar} = 10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa}$, so $P_{ext} = 1.2$ bar.
Final Answer: (A) 1.2 bar
Quick Tip: $1\ \mathrm{dm^3\,bar} = 100$ J, so $P = \frac{600}{5 \times 100} = 1.2$ bar directly; the number of moles is not needed.

questions.stem: Which from following tests confirms presence of aldehydic group in glucose?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Oxime formation only shows a carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone); penta acetate shows five OH groups.
Step 2: Bromine water is a mild oxidant that oxidises only an aldehyde group to COOH without changing the carbon chain: $\mathrm{CHO(CHOH)_4CH_2OH \xrightarrow{Br_2\ water} COOH(CHOH)_4CH_2OH}$ (gluconic acid). This proves the carbonyl group is an aldehyde.
Final Answer: (B) Formation of gluconic acid when reacted with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ water.
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{NH_2OH}$ = carbonyl present; $\mathrm{Br_2}$ water = that carbonyl is CHO.

options.text: Formation of oxime when reacted with $\mathrm{NH_2OH}$.
Formation of gluconic acid when reacted with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ water.
Formation of saccharic acid when glucose and gluconic acid treated with dil. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$.
Formation of penta acetate when treated with acetic anhydride.

questions.stem: Which metal in following compounds is not present in fractional oxidation state?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$, $\mathrm{Mn_3O_4}$ and $\mathrm{Pb_3O_4}$ the average oxidation state of the metal is $\frac{+8}{3}$ (fractional).
Step 2: In $\mathrm{Na_2S_4O_6}$ the metal is Na, which is $+1$. The fractional value ($+2.5$) belongs to sulphur, a non-metal.
Final Answer: (D) $\mathrm{Na_2S_4O_6}$
Quick Tip: Read the question carefully: it asks about the metal; in tetrathionate only S has a fractional average oxidation state.

questions.stem: Which among the following is NOT dicarboxylic acid?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Malonic acid $\mathrm{HOOC-CH_2-COOH}$, glutaric acid $\mathrm{HOOC(CH_2)_3COOH}$ and adipic acid $\mathrm{HOOC(CH_2)_4COOH}$ all have two COOH groups.
Step 2: Valeric acid is pentanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_3COOH}$, with only one COOH group (monocarboxylic).
Final Answer: (C) Valeric acid
Quick Tip: Dicarboxylic acids in order: oxalic, malonic, succinic, glutaric, adipic (\"Oh My Such Good Apple\").

questions.stem:
Identify the substrate ' X ' in the following reaction.
$\mathrm{X + \underset{(air)}{O_2} \xrightarrow[ii)\ dil\ HCl\ \Delta]{i)\ Co\text{-}naphenate\ 423\ K} Phenol + Acetone}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: This is the cumene process. Cumene (isopropyl benzene) is oxidised by air to cumene hydroperoxide: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH(CH_3)_2 + O_2 \rightarrow C_6H_5C(CH_3)_2OOH}$.
Step 2: Acid (dil. HCl) cleaves the hydroperoxide: $\mathrm{C_6H_5C(CH_3)_2OOH \xrightarrow{H^+} C_6H_5OH + CH_3COCH_3}$, giving phenol and acetone.
Final Answer: (D) Isopropyl benzene
Quick Tip: Phenol + acetone together as products always means the cumene process.

questions.stem: Identify the monomers use to prepare glyptal.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Glyptal is a polyester (alkyd resin) made by condensation polymerisation of ethylene glycol with phthalic acid.
Step 2: Ethylene glycol + terephthalic acid gives terylene (Dacron); $\beta$-hydroxybutyric + $\beta$-hydroxyvaleric acid gives PHBV.
Final Answer: (D) Ethylene glycol and phtalic acid
Quick Tip: Phthalic (ortho) acid gives glyptal; terephthalic (para) acid gives terylene.

questions.stem:
Identify the product ' $Z$ ' in the following series of reactions.
$\mathrm{Ethanol \xrightarrow[\Delta]{SOCl_2} X \xrightarrow[Dry\ ether]{Mg} Y \xrightarrow{NH_3} Z}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH + SOCl_2 \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl + SO_2 + HCl}$, so X is ethyl chloride.
Step 2: $\mathrm{C_2H_5Cl + Mg \xrightarrow{dry\ ether} C_2H_5MgCl}$, so Y is ethyl magnesium chloride.
Step 3: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ has acidic H, which protonates the Grignard reagent: $\mathrm{C_2H_5MgCl + NH_3 \rightarrow C_2H_6 + Mg(NH_2)Cl}$. So Z is ethane.
Final Answer: (D) Ethane
Quick Tip: Grignard reagent + any compound with active H ($\mathrm{H_2O}$, ROH, $\mathrm{NH_3}$) gives the alkane R-H.

questions.stem: Calculate the enthalpy of vaporisation of ethanol if 11.5 g of ethanol is completely vaporised by supplying 11.8 kJ of heat.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Molar mass of ethanol $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} = 46\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$, so moles $= \frac{11.5}{46} = 0.25$ mol.
Step 2: $\Delta_{vap}H = \frac{q}{n} = \frac{11.8}{0.25} = 47.2\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (B) $47.2\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Molar enthalpy = heat supplied / moles, not / grams.

questions.stem: Identify the reagent involved in Sandmeyer reaction.
questions.solution:
Step 1: In the Sandmeyer reaction, a diazonium salt is treated with a cuprous salt: $\mathrm{CuCl/HCl}$, $\mathrm{CuBr/HBr}$ or $\mathrm{CuCN/KCN}$.
Step 2: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- \xrightarrow{CuCN/KCN} C_6H_5CN + N_2}$. Cu powder/HBr is the Gattermann reaction; $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ or ethanol reduce the diazonium salt to benzene.
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{CuCN/KCN}$
Quick Tip: Sandmeyer uses cuprous salts; Gattermann uses copper powder with HX.

questions.stem: The solubility of AgBr is $7.1 \times 10^{-7}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$. Calculate its solubility product at the same temperature.
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{AgBr \rightleftharpoons Ag^+ + Br^-}$, so $K_{sp} = S^2$.
Step 2: $K_{sp} = (7.1 \times 10^{-7})^2 = 50.41 \times 10^{-14} = 5.04 \times 10^{-13}$
Final Answer: (D) $5.04 \times 10^{-13}$
Quick Tip: For 1:1 salts $K_{sp} = S^2$; square the mantissa and double the exponent.

questions.stem:
Identify the product ' B ' in the following sequence of reactions.
$\mathrm{Methylpropanoate \xrightarrow[dil.\ NaOH]{\Delta} A \xrightarrow[Conc.\ HCl]{H^+} B}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Alkaline hydrolysis (saponification): $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOCH_3 + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3CH_2COONa + CH_3OH}$, so A is sodium propanoate.
Step 2: Acidification: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COONa + HCl \rightarrow CH_3CH_2COOH + NaCl}$, so B is propanoic acid.
Final Answer: (D) propanoic acid
Quick Tip: Base hydrolysis of an ester gives the carboxylate salt; the free acid appears only after adding mineral acid.

questions.stem: Which from following functional groups has highest priority order for naming the poly functional compound?
questions.solution:
Step 1: IUPAC priority order: -COOH > -$\mathrm{SO_3H}$ > -COOR > -COX > $\mathrm{-CONH_2}$ > -CN > -CHO > C=O > -OH > $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ > C=C, $\mathrm{C\equiv C}$.
Step 2: Among the given groups the amide $\mathrm{-CONH_2}$ comes first, so it decides the suffix (-amide).
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{-CONH_2}$
Quick Tip: Acid derivatives (ester, acid halide, amide) outrank nitrile, which outranks aldehyde and ketone.

questions.stem:
Identify the product ' X ' formed in the following reaction,
Sodium ethoxide + Isopropyl chloride $\longrightarrow \mathrm{X} +$ Ethanol + Sodium chloride
questions.solution:
Step 1: Ethoxide is a strong base and isopropyl chloride is a secondary halide, so elimination (E2) dominates over substitution.
Step 2: $\mathrm{CH_3CHClCH_3 + C_2H_5ONa \rightarrow CH_3CH=CH_2 + C_2H_5OH + NaCl}$. The by-product ethanol shown in the equation confirms dehydrohalogenation; X is propene.
Final Answer: (C) Propene
Quick Tip: If ethanol forms as a product, ethoxide acted as a base (elimination), not as a nucleophile (ether).

questions.stem: Which among the following is NOT benzylic halide?
questions.solution:
Step 1: A benzylic halide has the halogen on the $\mathrm{sp^3}$ carbon directly attached to the benzene ring.
Step 2: In (A) $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2Br}$, (B) $\mathrm{C_6H_5CHBrCH_3}$ and (C) $\mathrm{C_6H_5CBr(CH_3)_2}$ the Br is on the ring-bearing carbon. In (D) $\mathrm{BrCH_2-CH(C_6H_5)-CH_2CH_3}$ the Br is on C-1 but the phenyl is on C-2, so it is not benzylic.
Final Answer: (D) 1-Bromo-2-phenylbutane
Quick Tip: Benzylic: halogen and phenyl on the same carbon locant.

questions.stem: If compressibility factor of real gas is 1.05 at STP. What is molar volume of real gas?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $Z = \frac{V_{real}}{V_{ideal}}$, and the ideal molar volume at STP is $22.4\ \mathrm{dm^3}$.
Step 2: $V_{real} = Z \times V_{ideal} = 1.05 \times 22.4 = 23.52\ \mathrm{dm^3}$
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{23.52\,dm^3}$
Quick Tip: $Z > 1$ means the real gas occupies more volume than the ideal gas (repulsions dominate).

questions.stem: Identify the type of defect from following in stainless steel.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Stainless steel is an alloy in which small carbon atoms occupy the interstitial (void) sites of the iron lattice.
Step 2: An impurity atom sitting in the voids of the host lattice is an interstitial impurity defect (brass is the standard example of substitutional impurity).
Final Answer: (B) Interstitial impurity defect
Quick Tip: Brass = substitutional impurity; steel/stainless steel = interstitial impurity (small C atoms).

questions.stem: Which from following is a lanthanoid element?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Lanthanoids are elements 58 (Ce) to 71 (Lu).
Step 2: Er (erbium, Z = 68) is a lanthanoid; Am (95), Np (93) and Lr (103) are actinoids.
Final Answer: (A) Er
Quick Tip: Elements named after research labs or physicists in the 90s-100s (Am, Np, Lr) are actinoids.

questions.stem: Which from following formulae is used to obtain value of $\mathrm{E_{cell}^{r}}$ for a reaction taking place in Dry cell?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{cell}$, so $E^\circ_{cell} = \frac{-\Delta G^\circ}{nF}$.
Step 2: Dry cell reaction: $\mathrm{Zn_{(s)} + 2MnO_{2(s)} + 2NH_4^+ \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + Mn_2O_{3(s)} + 2NH_3 + H_2O}$. Zn goes from 0 to +2, so $n = 2$ and $E^\circ_{cell} = \frac{-\Delta G^\circ}{2F}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{-\Delta G^\circ}{2F}$
Quick Tip: n = electrons transferred in the balanced cell reaction; for the Zn-based dry cell it is 2.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions exhibits highest freezing point depression?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta T_f = iK_f m$, so compare $i \times m$ (effective particle concentration).
Step 2: NaCl: $2 \times 0.1 = 0.2$; $\mathrm{MgSO_4}$: $2 \times 0.05 = 0.1$; $\mathrm{AlPO_4}$: $2 \times 1 = 2$; $\mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3}$: $5 \times 0.05 = 0.25$.
Step 3: The largest value is 2 for 1 m $\mathrm{AlPO_4}$, so it shows the highest depression.
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{1\,m\,AlPO_4}$
Quick Tip: Always multiply the van't Hoff factor by molality before comparing colligative properties.

questions.stem: Calculate the energy associated with third orbit of $\mathrm{He^+}$.
questions.solution:
Step 1: For a hydrogen-like ion, $E_n = -2.18 \times 10^{-18}\frac{Z^2}{n^2}\ \mathrm{J}$; for $\mathrm{He^+}$, $Z = 2$ and $n = 3$.
Step 2: $E_3 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{4}{9} = -0.969 \times 10^{-18} = -9.69 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$
Final Answer: (D) $-9.69 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$
Quick Tip: Energy scales as $Z^2/n^2$; do not forget $Z^2 = 4$ for $\mathrm{He^+}$.

questions.stem: What is the pH of buffer solution formed by mixing 0.01 M acetic acid and 0.05 M sodium acetate? $(\mathrm{pK_a} = 4.7447)$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Henderson equation: $\mathrm{pH = pK_a + \log\frac{[salt]}{[acid]}}$
Step 2: $\mathrm{pH} = 4.7447 + \log\frac{0.05}{0.01} = 4.7447 + \log 5 = 4.7447 + 0.6990 = 5.4437$
Final Answer: (C) 5.44
Quick Tip: More salt than acid means pH > $\mathrm{pK_a}$; this rules out (A) and (B) at once.

questions.stem: Identify the geometry of $\mathrm{TeF_4}$ molecule from the following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Te has 6 valence electrons; 4 form bonds with F and 2 remain as one lone pair, so there are 5 electron pairs ($sp^{3}d$ hybridisation).
Step 2: Five electron pairs are arranged trigonal bipyramidally (the lone pair takes an equatorial position, so the atoms alone form a see-saw shape). Among the options, the geometry is trigonal bipyramidal.
Final Answer: (C) Trigonal bipyramidal
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{AB_4E}$ (like $\mathrm{SF_4}$, $\mathrm{TeF_4}$): trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry, see-saw shape.

questions.topic: General Principles And Processes Of Isolation Of Elements
questions.stem: Which of the following set of elements is present in apatite?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Apatite is a calcium phosphate mineral, $\mathrm{Ca_5(PO_4)_3(F, Cl, OH)}$, e.g. fluorapatite $\mathrm{3Ca_3(PO_4)_2 \cdot CaF_2}$.
Step 2: So it contains Ca, P and O (the phosphate group); it has no Mg, Al or S.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{Ca, P}$ and O
Quick Tip: Apatite and phosphorite are the main ores of phosphorus (calcium phosphates).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not negatively charged sol?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Negatively charged sols include metal sulphides ($\mathrm{As_2S_3}$), clay, metals, starch and acid dyes like congo red.
Step 2: Haemoglobin (blood protein) sol is positively charged, like metal hydroxide sols and basic dyes.
Final Answer: (B) Haemoglobin
Quick Tip: Positive sols: metal hydroxides, haemoglobin, basic dyes (methylene blue).

questions.stem: The rate constant for the reaction, $\mathrm{2N_2O_{5(g)} \rightarrow 2N_2O_{4(g)} + O_{2(g)}}$ is $4.98 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. What is the order of reaction?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Units of k are $(\mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}})^{1-n}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ for an n-th order reaction.
Step 2: Here the unit is $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, so $1 - n = 0$ and $n = 1$: a first order reaction (decomposition of $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ is the standard first-order example).
Final Answer: (B) 1
Quick Tip: Zero order: $\mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$; first: $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; second: $\mathrm{dm^3\,mol^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$.

questions.stem: Identify thermoplastic polymer from following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Thermoplastics are linear or slightly branched polymers with intermediate intermolecular forces that soften on heating and harden on cooling repeatedly.
Step 2: Polyvinyl (chloride), PVC, is the standard thermoplastic. Bakelite is a cross-linked thermosetting polymer, terylene is classed as a fibre and neoprene as an elastomer.
Final Answer: (A) Polyvinyl
Quick Tip: Classification by forces: elastomers (weakest) < thermoplastics < fibres (strongest); thermosets are cross-linked.

questions.stem: What is the number of unpaired electrons in Ti in +3 state?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Ti (Z = 22): $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{2}4s^{2}$.
Step 2: $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$ loses the two 4s electrons and one 3d electron: $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{1}$, so it has 1 unpaired electron.
Final Answer: (C) 1
Quick Tip: Transition metals lose 4s electrons before 3d electrons.

questions.stem: Calculate the total number of tetrahedral and octahedral voids formed in 0.6 mol of a compound if it forms hcp structure.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Number of particles $N = 0.6 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 3.613 \times 10^{23}$
Step 2: In hcp, octahedral voids $= N$ and tetrahedral voids $= 2N$, so total voids $= 3N$.
Step 3: Total $= 3 \times 3.613 \times 10^{23} = 10.84 \times 10^{23} = 1.084 \times 10^{24}$
Final Answer: (C) $1.084 \times 10^{24}$
Quick Tip: Close packing of N spheres: N octahedral + 2N tetrahedral = 3N voids.

questions.stem: Calculate the concentration of dissolved gas in water at $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ if partial pressure of gas at same temperature is 0.15 atm . $\left[\mathrm{K_H = 0.15\ mol\,dm^{-3}\,atm^{-1}}\right]$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Henry's law (solubility form): $S = K_H \times P$
Step 2: $S = 0.15\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}\,atm^{-1}} \times 0.15\ \mathrm{atm} = 0.0225\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$
Final Answer: (D) 0.0225 M
Quick Tip: Check the units of $K_H$: $\mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}\,atm^{-1}}$ means multiply by pressure.

questions.stem: Which from following is an essential amino acid?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Essential amino acids cannot be synthesised by the body and must come from the diet.
Step 2: Histidine is essential (valine, leucine, isoleucine, lysine, threonine, methionine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, arginine, histidine). Tyrosine, serine and glycine are made in the body (non-essential).
Final Answer: (C) Histidine
Quick Tip: Mnemonic for essential amino acids: \"PVT TIM HALL\" (Phe, Val, Thr, Trp, Ile, Met, His, Arg, Leu, Lys).

questions.stem: What is the mass in grams of 0.25 mol water?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Molar mass of $\mathrm{H_2O} = 2(1) + 16 = 18\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Step 2: Mass $= n \times M = 0.25 \times 18 = 4.5$ g
Final Answer: (C) 4.5 g
Quick Tip: mass = moles × molar mass.

questions.stem: Which from following statements is correct regarding a detergent sodium lauryl sulphate?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Sodium lauryl sulphate is $\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_{11}OSO_3^-Na^+}$; its surface-active part is the long-chain anion, so it is an anionic detergent.
Step 2: Anionic detergents like sodium lauryl sulphate are used in toothpastes (and household cleaning); cationic detergents are used in hair conditioners; non-ionic (ether-type) ones in liquid dishwashing detergents.
Final Answer: (A) It is anionic detergent and is used in toothpaste.
Quick Tip: Sulphates/sulphonates = anionic; quaternary ammonium salts = cationic.

options.text: It is anionic detergent and is used in toothpaste.
It is cationic detergent and is used as household detergent.
It is cationic detergent and is used as hair conditioner.
It is an ether and used as liquid detergent.

questions.stem: Identify the structural formula of phloroglucinol.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Phloroglucinol is benzene-1,3,5-triol, a trihydric phenol with OH groups on alternate carbons.
Step 2: Structure (A) has OH at positions 1, 3 and 5. (B) is 1,2,3-triol (pyrogallol), (C) is 1,2,4-triol (hydroxyquinol) and (D) is 1,3-diol (resorcinol).
Final Answer: (A) benzene-1,3,5-triol structure
Quick Tip: Pyrogallol 1,2,3-; phloroglucinol 1,3,5- (symmetrical).

questions.stem:
Which of the following equations is correct regarding rate of disappearance of reactant and appearance of product for
$\mathrm{N_{2(g)} + 3H_{2(g)} \longrightarrow 2NH_{3(g)}}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Rate $= -\frac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{3}\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{NH_3}]}{dt}$
Step 2: From the last two terms: $\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{NH_3}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{3}\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt}$. Multiplying by 6: $3\frac{d[\mathrm{NH_3}]}{dt} = -2\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt}$
Step 3: (A) and (B) have wrong coefficients, and (C) lacks the minus sign (the reactant concentration decreases).
Final Answer: (D) $3\frac{\mathrm{d[NH_3]}}{\mathrm{dt}} = -2\frac{\mathrm{d[H_2]}}{\mathrm{dt}}$
Quick Tip: Reactant terms carry a minus sign; divide every rate by its coefficient.

questions.stem: If salicylic acid ( 138 u ) reacts with acetic anhydride ( 102 u ) to form aspirin ( 180 u ) calculate % atom economy.
questions.solution:
Step 1: % atom economy $= \frac{\text{formula weight of desired product}}{\text{sum of formula weights of all reactants}} \times 100$
Step 2: $= \frac{180}{138 + 102} \times 100 = \frac{180}{240} \times 100 = 75\%$
Final Answer: (D) $75\%$
Quick Tip: The other 25% of the mass leaves as the by-product acetic acid (60 u).

questions.stem: Identify a molecule having highest number of lone pair of electrons in valence shell of central atom.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Lone pairs on central atom $= \frac{\text{valence electrons} - \text{electrons used in bonds}}{2}$.
Step 2: $\mathrm{NH_3}$: $\frac{5-3}{2} = 1$; $\mathrm{SF_4}$: $\frac{6-4}{2} = 1$; $\mathrm{ICl_3}$: $\frac{7-3}{2} = 2$; $\mathrm{PCl_3}$: $\frac{5-3}{2} = 1$.
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{ICl_3}$
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{ICl_3}$ ($\mathrm{AB_3E_2}$) is T-shaped because of its two lone pairs.

questions.stem: Which among the following compounds has lowest boiling point?
questions.solution:
Step 1: All four have similar molar masses (73-74), so boiling point depends on hydrogen bonding.
Step 2: Propanoic acid (dimeric H-bonding) > n-butanol (strong O-H...O H-bond) > diethylamine (weaker N-H...N H-bond) > ethyldimethylamine, a tertiary amine with no H on N and hence no intermolecular H-bonding.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{C_2H_5N(CH_3)_2}$
Quick Tip: Among isomeric amines: $1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$ in boiling point.

questions.stem: Calculate the molar mass of an element if it forms fcc unit cell structure [mass of unit cell $= 1.8 \times 10^{-22}\ \mathrm{g}$, $\mathrm{N_A} = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ ]
questions.solution:
Step 1: For fcc, $n = 4$ atoms per unit cell, and mass of unit cell $= \frac{nM}{N_A}$.
Step 2: $M = \frac{\text{mass of unit cell} \times N_A}{n} = \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-22} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}}{4}$
Step 3: $M = \frac{108.4}{4} = 27.1 \approx 27.0\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (A) $27.0\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Atoms per cell: sc 1, bcc 2, fcc 4.

questions.stem: Calculate the osmotic pressure of 0.03 mole of non electrolyte solute dissolved in $\mathrm{0.1\,dm^3}$ of water at $300\ \mathrm{K}$. $\left[\mathrm{R = 0.082\ dm^3\,atm\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}\right]$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\pi = \frac{n}{V}RT$
Step 2: $\pi = \frac{0.03}{0.1} \times 0.082 \times 300 = 0.3 \times 24.6 = 7.38\ \mathrm{atm}$
Final Answer: (A) 7.4 atm
Quick Tip: With R in $\mathrm{dm^3\,atm}$ units, keep volume in $\mathrm{dm^3}$ and the answer comes out in atm.

questions.stem: Identify the correct decreasing order of stability of complexes formed by divalent metal ions with same ligand.
questions.solution:
Step 1: For metal ions of the same charge with the same ligand, complex stability increases with the charge-to-size ratio (smaller ion, higher stability); for first-row ions it follows $\mathrm{Mn^{2+} < Fe^{2+} < Co^{2+} < Ni^{2+} < Cu^{2+}}$ (Irving-Williams order).
Step 2: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ is the smallest and forms the most stable complexes; $\mathrm{Cd^{2+}}$, a much larger 4d ion, has the lowest charge-to-size ratio, so the textbook order is $\mathrm{Cu^{2+} > Ni^{2+} > Co^{2+} > Fe^{2+} > Mn^{2+} > Cd^{2+}}$.
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{Cu^{2+} > Mn^{2+} > Cd^{2+}}$
Quick Tip: State-board rule: same charge, same ligand, so the smaller ion gives the more stable complex; Cu(II) tops the Irving-Williams series.
